info.title: Vericairn API
info.description: One versioned API that every client uses. Authority is evaluated by the runtime behind it; a client presents, requests and observes. Every response is what the runtime observed, never what a client assumed. Problems carry a stable code (refused, rejected, not-found, invalid, denied, provider, conflict, reconcile-required), a message with the permitted next action and, for rejected records, the findings. Transports: a local socket (Unix domain socket, or a named pipe on Windows) authenticated by operating-system identity, and loopback TLS pinned to the runtime certificate where every request is signed by an admitted device (headers Vericairn-Device, Vericairn-Signed-At, Vericairn-Signature; scheme vericairn-request/1). From 0.6.0, when the operator configures an address, the local network: mutual TLS, where a paired device presents a certificate its device key issued, has the runtime identity it pinned at pairing sign the runtime certificate's fingerprint for each connection (GET /v1/runtime/identity, scheme vericairn-runtime-identity/1), and signs every request; the device must be admitted now and permitted the local-network profile, and acts for its own principal. A device pairs with a code an administrator issues (POST /v1/pairings), over POST /v1/pairing/hello and POST /v1/pairing/confirm (scheme vericairn-pairing/1).

post.summary: Issue a pairing code under an administrator's authority (the operator, or a principal with the administer scope whose admitted device here signs the admission) for a principal and the connectivity profiles its device will be permitted: 16 characters, 80 secret bits, for ten minutes, five attempts and one device. On the runtime's own machine only.

200.description: PairingIssued: the code, shown once, with the principal, the profiles, the expiry, the attempts, the address and the runtime identity's fingerprint.

409.description: No local-network profile is served, or too many codes wait (Problem).

422.description: Refused: an unknown principal or profile, no administrator's authority, or no admitted device of the administrator here to sign the admission (Problem).

post.summary: Start a pairing over the local network with a code's handle and a nonce: the runtime answers with its identity, the certificate on this connection, the device record it will write, and its MAC with the code's runtime key.

200.description: PairingChallenge: the runtime's identity, the certificate on this connection and the device record to sign, with the runtime's MAC; uses one of the code's attempts.

401.description: The code is unknown, expired, used or out of attempts, or the request did not come over the local network (Problem with code denied).

422.description: A hello without a handle or a nonce (Problem).

post.summary: Complete a pairing: the device's key, descriptive identity and signature of its record, with its MAC with the code's device key; the runtime records the device and its admission, and answers with its MAC over the whole exchange.

200.description: PairingCompleted: the device record and the admission, with the runtime's MAC over the exchange.

401.description: No such exchange is open, the code expired or was used, or the confirmation does not match the code (Problem with code denied); nothing is recorded.

422.description: The device's signature does not verify, or the estate refused its records (Problem, with findings when rejected); nothing is recorded.
